ready2_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: In the figure, ABCD is a rectangle and PQRS a square. The area of the grey part is half as big as the area of ABCD. How long is the side PX?
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: In the figure, ABCD is a rectangle and PQRS a square. The area of the grey part is half as big as the area of ABCD. How long is the side PX?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: It can be seen from the figure that ABCD is a rectangle, the bottom side DC is marked as 10, and the right side BC is marked as 6, so the area of rectangle ABCD is 10×6=60. In the figure, PQRS is a square, and the top side PQ is marked as 6, therefore the side length of the square is 6. The gray part is the overlapping part of the square and the rectangle; in the figure it is a rectangle, and its horizontal width is equal to the side length of the square, 6. The problem says that the area of the gray part is half of the area of rectangle ABCD, so the gray area is 60÷2=30. Thus the height of the gray rectangle is 30÷6=5. The total length of the square side PS is 6, and PX is the segment from P to the upper side of the rectangle, so PX=6-5=1.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as follows: ABCD is a rectangle with bottom side DC labeled 10 and right side BC labeled 6, so its area is 60. PQRS is a square with side PQ labeled 6, and its vertical sides intersect the top of the rectangle at X and Y. The grey region is the overlap of the square and rectangle; visually it is a rectangle with width XY equal to the square side, 6. From the text, the grey area is half the area of ABCD, so it is 30. Therefore the grey rectangle’s height XS is 30/6=5. Since the square side PS is 6 and PS is split into PX plus XS, PX=6-5=1.
